content: Approximately 120 million women worldwide are affected by Trichomonas vaginalis vaginitis annually. This infection is transmitted sexually and is thought to increase the risk of HIV transmission. The objective of this review was to evaluate the effectiveness of various treatment strategies for trichomoniasis in women. To gather relevant studies, searches were conducted in the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, MEDLINE, and EMBASE. Additional trials were identified through reference lists of reviews, pharmaceutical companies, and informal methods. Only published data were included in the review, with the most recent search conducted in November 2002. The review included randomized or quasi-randomized trials that compared different treatment strategies for women with trichomoniasis. Eligible studies included those comparing different antitrichomonal drugs or doses, as well as studies comparing treatment to no treatment or placebo. The quality of the trials was assessed, and data were independently extracted by two reviewers using standardized criteria. A total of 54 trials were included in the review. Nitroimidazole drugs were found to be effective in achieving parasitological cure during short-term follow-up. Additionally, treating sexual partners was shown to be effective in reducing reinfection rates over the longer term. The authors concluded that a single oral dose of nitroimidazole is sufficient to achieve parasitological cure. However, further research is needed to develop effective strategies for treating sexual partners in order to prevent reinfections and reduce the overall prevalence of trichomoniasis.
